text: Windows says nine hundred thirty-one gigabytes. Nothing's missing.
Drive makers count in powers of ten:
a terabyte is one trillion bytes.
Windows counts in powers of two:
its gigabyte is one billion, seventy-three million, seven hundred forty-one thousand, eight hundred twenty-four bytes.
Divide a trillion by that, and you get nine hundred thirty-one.
The binary unit even has its own name,
the gibby-byte, but almost nobody uses it.
So a two-terabyte drive shows one thousand, eight hundred sixty-two.
